newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu heads back to Israel.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu heads back to Israel.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu headed home on Sunday after a two-day visit to New York City, where he worshipped at a synagogue and met with the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations and Jewish leaders.

Security was so tight that the departure of Netanyahu, his wife and other members of his entourage from a special security hanger at John F. Kennedy International Airport was not announced until the jet was airborne.
The plane lifted off at 4:45 p.m. EST (2145 GMT), said a spokeswoman for the Port Authority that operates the three major airports in the city.

Netanyahu's entourage was delayed when a police motorcycle escort was involved in an accident en route to the airport. The officer, whose name was not released, suffered head injuries and was in stable condition at a local hospital.

Netanyahu met with President Bill Clinton and other U.S. officials in Washington last week to discuss ways to generate Middle East peace momentum after Israel's withdrawal of troops from Hebron in the West Bank.

After sabbath observance, Netanyahu met late on Saturday with Bill Richardson, the new U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, who said they discussed ways to increase Israel's participation at the United Nations.

In a brief speech at the Fifth Avenue Synagogue, where he once worshipped as Israel's U.N. envoy, Netanyahu invited the congregation to Israel to celebrate his country's 50th anniversary as a nation next year.
